reasons: Reviewer recommends rejection: [fr page] All checked facts match the cited sources; no factual fix needed. Remaining issue is style only: the page mirrors the English structure sentence by sentence.

claims.claim: Born Lonnie Rashid Lynn Jr., 13 March 1972, Chicago, Illinois
claims.note: Grammy artist page gives birth name, date and place; TV Academy gives March 13 and Chicago, Illinois.

claims.claim: First rapper to win a Grammy, an Oscar and an Emmy
claims.note: Article headline and text: first rapper to take home a GRAMMY, an Oscar, and an Emmy.

claims.claim: Like Water for Chocolate is his fourth studio album and a career high; quoted 'one of the greatest times in my life'
claims.note: Interview calls it his fourth album and a major career high; English original is 'Man, this was one of the greatest times in my life'. The Spanish, Portuguese, German and French quotes are faithful renderings.

claims.claim: Album title comes from a film whose concept was people cooking and showing love
claims.note: Interview describes the film concept. The article gives no year, so nothing is contradicted.

claims.claim: 'The Light' was the album's first hit and his first song on mainstream radio
claims.note: Interview: 'That was the first song that I had on the radio, on mainstream radio'.

claims.claim: 'The Light' nominated Best Rap Solo Performance, 2001
claims.note: Grammy artist page lists 2001 Best Rap Solo Performance for The Light (nominee).

claims.claim: Femi Kuti appears on the album; getting him was 'incredible'
claims.note: Interview: Femi Kuti on the album, Common calls it incredible.

claims.claim: 'Geto Heaven' was made for D'Angelo; D'Angelo wanted 'Chicken Grease' and offered something in return; Common got D'Angelo onto 'Geto Heaven'
claims.note: Interview states each point.

claims.claim: 'Chicken Grease' would have fitted Common's own work like 'Cold Blooded' before it ended on D'Angelo's Voodoo
claims.note: Interview: Chicken Grease would have fit 'the same lane as Cold Blooded'; it ended on Voodoo.

claims.claim: Questlove sequenced the album and executive-produced it
claims.note: Interview: Questlove sequenced the album and 'truly executive-produced' it.

claims.claim: A&R Wendy Goldstein introduced him to his acting coach
claims.note: Interview: 'My A&R Wendy Goldstein actually introduced me to my acting coach'.

claims.claim: Glory won Best Original Song at the 87th Academy Awards, credited to John Stephens and Lonnie Lynn
claims.note: Oscars.org: Glory from Selma, music and lyric by John Stephens and Lonnie Lynn, 87th Academy Awards (22 Feb 2015).

claims.claim: Glory won the 2015 Golden Globe for Best Original Song
claims.note: TV Academy: 2015 Best Original Song winner, Glory from Selma.

claims.claim: At the 2016 Grammys Glory was nominated for Best Rap Song and Best Rap/Sung Collaboration and won Best Song Written for Visual Media
claims.note: Grammy artist page lists all three entries with those statuses.

claims.claim: Played civil rights leader James Bevel in Selma (2014)
claims.note: TV Academy film credits: Selma (2014), as James Bevel.

claims.claim: 2017 Primetime Emmy for Outstanding Original Music and Lyrics for 'Letter to the Free' from 13th (Netflix)
claims.note: TV Academy lists the 2017 win for 13th, Netflix platform not separately stated but song credited to 13th.

claims.claim: Shared the Emmy with Robert Glasper and Karriem Riggins
claims.note: Article: Common shared the honor with Robert Glasper and Karriem Riggins.

claims.claim: One Emmy nomination in total, which was the win
claims.note: TV Academy: 1 nomination, 1 win.

claims.claim: The Emmy left him one Tony from EGOT, a club of 13 members at that time
claims.note: Article: one Tony win away from the so-called EGOT, an elite club with only 13 members so far.

claims.claim: Grammy Best Rap Album nominations: Be (2006), Finding Forever (2008), Universal Mind Control (2010), Nobody's Smiling (2015), The Auditorium, Vol. 1 (2025)
claims.note: All five appear as Best Rap Album nominees with those years.

claims.claim: Southside listed for 2008 in Best Rap Performance by a Duo or Group
claims.note: Grammy artist page: 2008 nominee.

claims.claim: Totals of three wins and 22 nominations
claims.note: Grammy artist page: 3 wins, 22 nominations.

claims.claim: Filmography (Smokin' Aces through Smallfoot) and narration of Bouncing Cats
claims.note: All listed credits appear on the TV Academy page, including Bouncing Cats (narrator).

claims.claim: Pete Rock and Common first worked together nearly 30 years earlier on 'The Bitch In Yoo' (1996); The Auditorium, Vol. 1 is both artists' first full-length release since 2021
claims.note: Complex article states both points.

claims.claim: Common has said there may be a second volume
claims.note: Complex reports Common telling People that there may be a second volume. The quote originates with People, so the citation is secondhand but accurate.

claims.claim: The Auditorium, Vol. 1 nominated for Best Rap Album (2025); 'When the Sun Shines Again' nominated for Best Rap Performance
claims.note: Both 2025 nominations listed.

claims.claim: Love of My Life won the 2003 Best R&B Song Grammy and was his first career Grammy
claims.note: TV Academy lists it as 2003 winner; Grammy artist page quotes the bio saying it was his first career GRAMMY.

claims.claim: Southside is a Grammy win listed without a year by the TV Academy, but not marked as a win on the Grammy artist page, so the win is disputed
claims.note: The two sources disagree as the article says; the page correctly labels it disputed rather than picking one.

valueNote: Adds the disputed Southside win, the EGOT remark and interview detail from the Recording Academy that the usual top results do not carry.
summary: [fr page] All checked facts match the cited sources; no factual fix needed. Remaining issue is style only: the page mirrors the English structure sentence by sentence.
